record.paper_title: Local and Global Methods in Data Mining: Basic Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: For mixture modeling methods used in data mining, determine what can be proved about the computational complexity of the mixture-modeling problem.

evidence.quote: Problem 4 Can anything be said about computational complexity of the mixture modeling problem?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the mixture modeling problem in the following form. Given a finite data set $X = \{x_1, \ldots, x_n\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, a family $\mathcal{F}$ of parametric probability density functions on $\mathbb{R}^d$ (for example multivariate Gaussians), and a positive integer $k$, find parameters $\theta_1, \ldots, \theta_k$ and nonnegative mixing weights $\pi_1, \ldots, \pi_k$ with $\sum_{j=1}^{k} \pi_j = 1$ that maximize the log-likelihood
$$L(\theta, \pi) \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{n} \log \!\left( \sum_{j=1}^{k} \pi_j\, f(x_i \mid \theta_j) \right), \qquad f(\cdot \mid \theta_j) \in \mathcal{F}.$$
Establish rigorous results on the computational complexity of this problem. Specifically, determine whether the mixture-modeling problem (in natural decision or optimization formulations) is NP-hard, characterize the parameter regimes (e.g., dependence on $n$, $d$, $k$, separation between components, and the choice of family $\mathcal{F}$) in which it is tractable or intractable, and identify approximation thresholds for computing a mixture whose log-likelihood is within a prescribed factor of the optimum.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent to the question being raised, several hardness results have been established. Maximum-likelihood estimation for mixtures of spherical Gaussians has been shown to be NP-hard, and there are hardness-of-learning results for Gaussian mixtures (e.g., reductions from learning parities with noise, and SQ lower bounds). Polynomial-time algorithms exist for learning well-separated or smoothed mixtures (Dasgupta; Vempala–Wang; Moitra–Valiant; Belkin–Sinha; Kalai–Moitra–Valiant). A complete complexity-theoretic characterization of the general mixture-modeling problem (across all families and regimes) is not available, so the broader question is only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: You probably don't have a general algorithm for an MLE of Gaussian mixtures
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of NP-hardness of MLE for Gaussian mixture models and the practical implications.
status_evidence.claim: MLE for Gaussian mixtures is computationally hard in general, partially answering the complexity question.

status_evidence.title: On the Hardness of Sampling from Mixture Distributions via Langevin Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes regimes in which Langevin dynamics fail to recover all components of sub-Gaussian mixtures within sub-exponential time.
status_evidence.claim: Recent hardness results address sampling/learning complexity of mixture models in specific regimes.
